text:
sophia: Quick share — ran a targeted perf sweep on the admission + KV-prefetch path this morning. Found an odd regression when kernel-choice flips at mid-batch.
cheng: ok curious — regression where exactly? p95/p99 or throughput? :thinking:
marcus: pinging the profiling data. are you running with prefetch enabled? we just tweaked the batcher heuristic yesterday.
sophia: yes prefetch=on, admission_mode=adaptive, microbatch_target=8. Observed stable throughput but p99 spikes around 3% of requests when sequence_len ~ 600-900.
ion: can you paste the flame or a snippet? even a short perflog helps.
sophia: pasted snippet below from perf-bench (trimmed):
```
# kernels: attn_fused_v2 -> fallback_kernel
seq_len  tokens  p50_ms p95_ms p99_ms  gpu_util
256        80     18     35     48      62%
512        60     32     78     110     81%
768        35     60     220    360     94%  <-- tail
1024       12     120    420    880     98%  <-- big tail and kernel fallback
```
sophia: note the kernel switch at ~768 leads to fallback path hitting massive latency and u99s; admission didn't shed those until late.
cheng: aha. so the runtime picks an optimized kernel up to 512, then a different path for >=768 that pushes activation memory and forces a slower kernel + KV cache misses?
marcus: that matches my local repro. The fallback path re-materializes KV slices because our prefetch window assumes kernel A's layout. When kernel B is used, we get memory thrash and extra memcpy.
perf-bot: alert — regression detected: kvcache-prefetch-layout-mismatch (regression id: reg-2028-04-12-42)
ion: two axes: (1) avoid kernel flip inside a microbatch, (2) make prefetch layout kernel-agnostic. Which is cheaper? Also admission could pre-check seq histogram and reject/buffer before flip.
sophia: my experiments: forcing uniform kernel by clipping microbatch to same seq_len bin (i.e., split larger microbatches) reduces p99 by ~60% but reduces throughput 8%.
cheng: that sounds like headroom vs saturation tradeoff. If we clamp microbatch to avoid kernel heterogeneity, we increase scheduling overhead / lost batching efficiency.
marcus: alternative: detect candidate requests that would trigger kernel B and prioritize them for dedicated slot with slightly reduced batch size — so we keep throughput but isolate tail.
ion: could we add a tiny heuristic at admission that checks the max_seq in the batch and if > threshold, do one of: preempt split, apply admission token_budget, or route to slow-path pool? 
sophia: I prototyped admission rule "reject_if_prob_flip>0.7" where prob_flip estimated from histogram over last 2m. Result: p99 improved, but we started seeing 429s for some customers — need graceful fallback.
marcus: graceful fallback could be enqueue-on-fast-path with backpressure token that drains when headroom exists, rather than outright reject.
cheng: also consider making kernel-selection deterministic per-model-version so we can design prefetch layout for that kernel. But that reduces kernel flexibility.
perf-bot: repro command appended: `./run_perf --model=resnet-llm --seq-hist=live --prefetch=1 --admission=adaptive --profile=kv` 
sophia: logging some traces here:
```
[trace] req-781: seq=820, batch_id=3421, chosen_kernel=fallback_kernel, kv_prefetch_layout=layout_v1 -> mismatch -> memcpy(2.4ms) -> stall(84ms)
[trace] req-782: seq=810, batch_id=3421, chosen_kernel=optimized_kernel, kv_prefetch_layout=layout_v1 -> ok
```
ion: we should add a microbenchmark that simulates mixed-kernel microbatches and measure memcpy penalties. If penalty > X then admission should avoid mixing.
marcus: agree. Also add a canary where we prefer kernel that keeps kv layout compatibility even if slightly slower per-token; it's better for p99.
cheng: ops considerations — if we start doing more routing to slow-path pools, capacity needs to be reserved (headroom). who's going to crank the reserved cap? cc @devops-bot ?
devops-bot: noted. I can spin up a low-priority pool for canary traffic. Will need an autoscale policy for slow-path with min=2 GPUs and burst up to 6. ETA 3 hours.
sophia: next steps proposal:
- add microbenchmark for mixed-kernel memcpy penalty (cheng)
- implement admission prob_flip heuristic as opt-in flag + enqueue-backpressure (sophia)
- evaluate kernel-determinism tradeoff on a single model version (marcus)
- add canary slow-path pool and run 48h regen (ion + devops-bot)
- update perf dashboards to show kernel-mix ratios and kv-prefetch-mismatch rate (perf)
cheng: I'll own benchmark and a PR that outputs CSV like `seq_bin,max_seq,memcpy_ms,p99_ms,gpu_util` so we can iterate.
sophia: cool. Anyone object to making this the default admission behavior? if not, we'll gate behind a rollout flag for 2 weeks.
marcus: no objections. prefer rollout with 10% tenants first.
ion: +1. Also add alert when mismatch_rate > 0.5% and p99 > target.
sophia: thanks all — I'll open issues/PRs and tag everyone. :rocket:
devops-bot: canary pool created: pool-id: slow-canary-17; monitor at https://grafana/internal/d/slow-canary-17
marcus: leaving a note: docs for model ops need a section on kernel layout assumptions. we'll capture that in model-onboarding checklist.
sophia: done — PRs incoming.
